images.title: Same factor keeps the shape
images.purpose: Shows that halving both sides of a 60 mm by 40 mm picture keeps its shape, while taking 20 mm off both sides stretches it.
images.composition: Three plain rectangles drawn to one scale: rectangle A in the centre left, rectangle C to its upper right and rectangle B to its lower right, each joined to A by one arrow. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Rectangle A is 60 units wide and 40 units high, outlined and filled in teal (#0072B2), with the label 'A 60 by 40' under it. Rectangle C is 30 units wide and 20 units high, filled in green (#009E73), with the label 'C 30 by 20' under it and the label 'same shape' beside it. Rectangle B is 40 units wide and 20 units high, filled in vermilion (#D55E00), with the label 'B 40 by 20' under it and the label 'stretched' beside it. One green arrow goes from A to C with the label '× 1/2 both sides'. One vermilion arrow goes from A to B with the label '− 20 both sides'. All lengths are in millimetres; no unit text is drawn. Exactly 3 rectangles, 2 arrows, no pictures inside the rectangles.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Multiplying both sides by the same factor keeps the shape; taking off the same amount does not.
images.description: Shows that halving both sides of a 60 mm by 40 mm picture keeps its shape, while taking 20 mm off both sides stretches it.
images.context: A to C: 60 ÷ 2 = 30, 40 ÷ 2 = 20. A to B: 60 − 20 = 40, 40 − 20 = 20; width factor 2/3, height factor 1/2.
images.teaching_notes: Draw the rectangles to the stated proportions exactly; B must visibly look wider for its height than A.

image_decisions.why: The contrast between same factor and same difference is the whole idea of this concept, and seeing the three rectangles to scale makes it obvious.
